outline.summary: Positions involvement as the prerequisite category for presence/immersion within a three-tier attentional hierarchy (attention -> involvement -> presence/immersion). States that the chapter will give a brief outline of the research process, the theoretical considerations bearing on the model's structure, and the model's constituent parts.

Compresses three years of qualitative research on World of Warcraft (Blizzard 2004) and Planetside (SOE 2003) into one page: extended personal participation, focus groups, twenty-five in-depth semi-structured interviews with experienced players recruited in-game, two sessions of up to two hours each, conducted within the virtual environment, supported by academic discussion, online-forum monitoring, blog tracking, and machinima viewing. Iterative coding between interviews; clusters of salient themes generated the six dimensions. Forebears named: T. L. Taylor 2006, Steinkuehler 2005, Klastrup 2004.

Distinguishes micro-involvement (in-session, moment-of-playing) from macro-involvement (longer-term motivational and off-line). Worked example: Empire: Total War (Creative Assembly 2009) — in-session army control = micro; bedtime tactical replay and commute campaign-planning = macro. States the 6-dimensions x 2-phases grid; dimensions are derived as 'clusters of emphasis' from interview data and are layered + transparent rather than discrete (one dimension changes the perception of the others without occluding them).

Builds the macro phase on Poels 2009's observation that game-experience research focuses too narrowly on the moment of gameplay. Pregame and postgame thinking, plans, expectations, community participation, anticipation, and motivation to return are the macro phase's content. Cites Poels et al. 2010's 'postgame experiences' focus-group findings as corroboration. Examples span all six dimensions (e.g. recalling avatar-control feats = kinesthetic; aesthetic-environment recollection = spatial + affective; clan-website work = shared). Figure 3.1 appears here — the radial diagram of the model.

Pivots to in-session moment-to-moment engagement. Grounds attention as the prior category to involvement (Fan et al. 2002), introduces attentional-capacity limits (Baddeley + Hitch 1994; Sturm + Willmes 2001), and uses this to explain internalization: learned tasks become automatic and free attentional resources for other dimensions. Differentiates attention-to-medium from active player input via Aarseth 1997's ergodicity. Develops the chapter's strongest theoretical move: ergodic effort is first and foremost a disposition / readiness to act, not merely physical input. Worked examples: Red Orchestra sniper waiting on a covered street (Figure 3.2); WoW Ratchet-to-Feathermoon map-planning. Cybernetic-circuit concept invoked via Dovey + Kennedy 2006.

outline.section: The Dimensions of the Player Involvement Model — Kinesthetic
outline.summary: Defines kinesthetic involvement as all modes of avatar / game-piece control, ranging from learning controls to fluency of internalized movement. Foregrounded when controls 'make themselves present' (unmastered, or demand complex sequences). Defers full development to Ch.4.

Engagement with spatial qualities of a virtual environment in terms of spatial control, navigation, and exploration. Accounts for the process of internalizing game spaces such that players sense inhabiting a place rather than perceiving a representation of space. Full development deferred to Ch.5.

Engagement from awareness of and interaction with other agents (human- or computer-controlled): cohabitation, cooperation, competition. Includes collaborative battle-strategy formation, guild-political discussion, ambient awareness that actions occur in social context. Full development deferred to Ch.6.

Engagement with both scripted story elements and story elements emergent from player interaction with the game world, its embedded objects, inhabitants, and ongoing events. Full development deferred to Ch.7.

Emotional engagement ranging from the calming sensation of an aesthetically pleasing scene to the adrenaline rush of competitive FPS rounds to the uncanny of an eerie action-horror episode. Accounts for rhetorical strategies of affect designed into the game and those precipitated by individual interpretation. Full development deferred to Ch.8.

Engagement with choices and their repercussions; goals stipulated by the game, established by the player, or decided by the player community; spur-of-the-moment decisions; opportunity-cost emphasis in well-balanced game systems. Full development deferred to Ch.9.

States that the dimensions need not all be present at high intensity in every game: Pong (Atari 1972) has low spatial involvement; The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (Bethesda 2006) and Half-Life 2 (Valve 2004) have high spatial involvement. Reads the model's diagram: outer edge = full attentional resources to a dimension; narrowing inward triangles = internalization (less attentional resource cost); further toward center = multiple dimensions simultaneously attended to. Uses the kinesthetic-control-internalization sequence as paradigm example. Closes with the modular + scalable claim — each dimension is a broad category that can be further subdivided.

Opens the chapter's negative-definitional excision. States the magic circle (Huizinga 1955) has been excluded from the model, then explains why. Reviews Salen + Zimmerman 2003's adoption of the concept (closed/playform/cultural schemata, with the cultural schema as the only open one), critiques their attempt to keep Huizinga while abandoning his apartness thesis. Invokes Ehrmann 1968's anti-Huizinga argument that 'reality' cannot be bracketed against play because play is an intractable manifestation of reality. Cites Taylor 2006 on the grounded-analytic cost of magic-circle bracketing.

Engages Juul 2005's spatial-formal reading of the magic circle: physical games have a spatial perimeter delineating the larger-world subset where game rules apply; digital games locate the circle in the screen and input devices. Calleja refuses this: in digital games the only space one can act in is the navigable space of the virtual environment, so the magic circle's spatial-marker function is redundant. Examples: FIFA 2009 stadium stands and Battlefield 1942 outside-combat-area as non-navigable representational backdrop.

Engages Suits 1978's lusory-attitude concept — players voluntarily adopt inefficient (rule-restricted) means to a goal. Calleja refuses on two grounds: (1) digital games enforce rules mechanically, so there is no need for the player to voluntarily adopt the inefficient means (the digital-golf counter-example); (2) Suits's argument is circular (games require the lusory attitude; the lusory attitude is what happens during a game). Cites Malaby 2007 on the logical incoherence of using 'play' as both mode-of-experience and form-of-activity, and Taylor 2006 + Pargman + Jakobsson 2006 + Copier 2007 on ethnographic findings against experiential bracketing. States the empirical finding: in his own interview data he found no indication that players enter a game-specific experiential mode.

Excises the fun-essentialism inherited from Huizinga via Crawford 2003, Koster 2005, Salen + Zimmerman 2003. Two arguments: (1) per Malaby 2007 + Dibbell 2006 + Taylor 2006, the fun=games equation imposes a normative status that ignores variation in experiential states, particularly when MMOG players engage willingly in tedious or laborious activity (Steinkuehler 2005; Yee 2006a, 2006b); (2) fun is analytically empty — it merely names a clustering of positive emotions without describing what they are or where they originate. Closes by reframing Huizinga's claim that fun resists analysis as a confession of the term's fuzziness, and recommits to the model's resolution of game experience into involvement-dimensions rather than essentialist labels.

concepts.label: player involvement model (PIM)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: A two-axis grid of six dimensions of involvement (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, affective, ludic) cross-cut by a temporal-phase distinction (macro / micro), organized as layered and transparent rather than discrete categories.

concepts.label: involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The pre-immersive category of player engagement that itself rests on attention; a more analytically tractable substitute for the catchall 'fun' and a prerequisite for the higher-order experiential phenomenon of presence/immersion.

concepts.label: three-tier attentional hierarchy (attention -> involvement -> presence/immersion)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's stratification of player-experiential categories: attention is the precondition of involvement; involvement is the precondition of presence/immersion; the lower stratum must be modeled before the higher can be analyzed.

concepts.label: macro phase / macro-involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Off-line involvement with the game: pre-session and post-session thinking, planning, anticipation, community participation, and motivation to return; the longer-term contextualization of the moment of gameplay.

concepts.label: micro phase / micro-involvement (in ludo res)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: In-session, moment-to-moment engagement during the act of play; ergodically active in the dispositional sense; attentionally structured by the same six dimensions but on a finer temporal grain.

concepts.label: dimensions as layered + transparent
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The six dimensions are not discrete bins but operate as layered, mutually permeating modulations of experience: each dimension changes the perception of the others without occluding them; their inclusion or exclusion alters how the others operate.

concepts.label: modular + scalable model structure
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Property of the PIM whereby dimensions combine fluidly across the diagram during play, and each dimension is itself a broad category capable of further subdivision into constituent components in subsequent chapters.

concepts.label: attention as cognitive-resource substrate
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Concentration of mental resources on stimuli — the underlying capacity-limited substrate for all involvement; foregrounded only when tasks exceed routine capacity (Fan et al. 2002; Baddeley + Hitch 1994; Sturm + Willmes 2001).

concepts.label: internalization of attentional load
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Process by which a learned task becomes automatic and ceases to consume the limited attentional resource, freeing capacity for other dimensions; paradigmatically illustrated by the passage from conscious control-learning to fluent kinesthetic engagement.

concepts.label: ergodicity as disposition / readiness to act
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's reformulation of Aarseth's ergodic input: the ergodic effort that constitutes gameplay is first and foremost a dispositional readiness to act, not merely the physical pressing of buttons; cognitive effort and patient alertness count as ergodic.

concepts.label: cybernetic circuit
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: The Dovey + Kennedy 2006 figure for the player-machine loop: hardware + representational layer + rules + environment constitute a feedback circuit within which ergodic input takes effect.

concepts.label: kinesthetic involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with avatar / game-piece control, ranging from learning the controls to internalized fluency of movement; foregrounded when controls 'make themselves present' through unmastery or demanded complex sequences.

concepts.label: spatial involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with the spatial qualities of a virtual environment via spatial control, navigation, and exploration; the internalizing of game-space such that the player senses inhabiting a place rather than perceiving a representation of space.

concepts.label: shared involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with other agents (human- or computer-controlled) under the modalities of cohabitation, cooperation, and competition; including ambient awareness that one's actions occur in a social context.

concepts.label: narrative involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with both story elements scripted into the game and emergent stories generated by ongoing interaction with the world, its embedded objects, inhabitants, and events.

concepts.label: affective involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with emotional states ranging from calming aesthetic response through adrenaline-rush competitive arousal to the uncanny of action-horror; accounting for both designer-installed rhetorical strategies of affect and player-precipitated affective interpretations.

concepts.label: ludic involvement
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Engagement with choices and their repercussions across game-stipulated, player-stipulated, and community-stipulated goals; opportunity cost is constitutive of well-balanced ludic systems.

concepts.label: magic-circle excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's deliberate exclusion of the Huizinga / Salen+Zimmerman / Juul magic-circle concept from the PIM, on two grounds: spatial redundancy in digital games (where only navigable virtual space can be acted in) and empirical absence of any game-specific experiential bracketing in his interview data.

concepts.label: lusory-attitude excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's refusal of Suits's lusory-attitude criterion (voluntary adoption of inefficient rule-restricted means) on the grounds that digital games enforce rules mechanically and on the grounds of the criterion's circularity.

concepts.label: fun-essentialism excision
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's rejection of the fun=games equation on the grounds that fun imposes a normative status that ignores variation across players' experiential states (including MMOG labor and tedium) and is analytically empty as a category.

concepts.label: Wittgensteinian family-resemblance reasoning
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Carried over from Ch.1: the refusal of essentialist definitions of games / play and the corresponding allowance that the PIM dimensions need not all be present at high intensity for every member of the game family.

concepts.label: grounded-theoretic qualitative methodology
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's research-process design: extended personal participation in two MMOGs, 25 in-game semi-structured interviews (two sessions, up to two hours each, conducted within the virtual environment), focus groups, online-forum monitoring, blog tracking, machinima review, iterative coding between interviews — clusters of salient themes generate the six dimensions.

concepts.label: postgame experiences
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Poels et al. 2010's term for thinking, recollection, and motivational residue following a gameplay session; cited by Calleja as empirical corroboration of the macro phase.

concepts.label: in ludo res (in the midst of the game)
concepts.definition_paraphrastic: Calleja's tag for the micro-phase analytical lens — the moment-to-moment engagement of the act of play, the temporal location from which all six dimensions are immediately operative.

positions.claim: Involvement is the prior analytical category to presence and immersion; both higher-order experiential phenomena rest on a well-modeled involvement substrate, just as involvement itself rests on attention.
positions.critique_target: Murray 1997 'deep immersion' + Ryan 2001 'spatial/temporal/emotional immersion' + presence-theory (Lombard, Witmer, Slater) — treated in Ch.2 as having skipped the involvement layer

positions.claim: Player experience is structured by two temporal phases — macro (off-line) and micro (in-session) — each of which the six dimensions operate within at a distinct temporal grain.
positions.critique_target: Game-experience research focused exclusively on the moment of gameplay (Poels 2009 cited approvingly as corroborator of the macro phase)

positions.claim: The six dimensions are layered and transparent rather than discrete; one dimension changes the perception of the others without occluding them, and the inclusion or exclusion of any one alters how the others operate.
positions.critique_target: Implicit critique of categorical / taxonomic readings of player experience

positions.claim: Ergodicity is first and foremost a disposition / readiness to act, not the physical pressing of an input device; cognitive effort and patient alertness are equally ergodic.
positions.critique_target: Implicit reframing of Aarseth 1997's ergodic-input formulation in the direction of dispositional / phenomenological action-readiness

positions.claim: The magic circle (Huizinga / Salen+Zimmerman / Juul) is redundant for digital games as a spatial marker and empirically unsupported as an experiential bracket; it is excluded from the model.
Suits's lusory attitude is inapplicable to digital games (which enforce rules mechanically, removing the voluntary adoption of inefficient means) and is circularly defined.

Fun is not the essence of play and is analytically empty as a category; it imposes a normative status that obscures the variation in experiential states (including MMOG labor and tedium) that engagement covers.

Applying the PIM does not require every dimension to be equally relevant to every game (Pong vs. Oblivion / Half-Life 2 on spatial intensity); the model is Wittgensteinian-permissive about family-resemblance distribution.
positions.critique_target: Implicit critique of essentialist game-definition projects

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement with avatar or game-piece control in a virtual environment, spanning from conscious learning of the controls through to fluent internalized movement; foregrounded when the controls make themselves present, either through unmastery or because a situation demands a complex sequence of actions that taxes the player.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 p.43 dimension paragraph; supplemented by the internalization passage at p.45

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement with the spatial qualities of a virtual environment via spatial control, navigation, and exploration; accounts for the process of internalizing game-spaces so that the player senses inhabiting a place rather than merely perceiving a representation of space.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 p.43 dimension paragraph

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement deriving from awareness of and interaction with other agents (human- or computer-controlled) in the game environment under the modalities of cohabitation, cooperation, and competition; encompasses collaborative strategy, guild-political discussion, and ambient awareness that one's actions occur in a social context.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 p.43 dimension paragraph

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement with both story elements scripted into the game and story elements emergent from the player's ongoing interaction with the game world, its embedded objects, its inhabitants, and the events that occur there.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 pp.43-44 dimension paragraph

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement with the range of emotional states elicited by play — from the calming sensation of an aesthetically pleasing scene through the adrenaline rush of competitive first-person-shooter rounds to the uncanny of an action-horror episode — including both designer-installed rhetorical strategies of affect and player-precipitated affective interpretations.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 p.44 dimension paragraph

dimension_operational_definitions.definition_text: Engagement with choices and their repercussions, where choices may be directed toward game-stipulated, player-stipulated, or community-stipulated goals, may be made on the spur of the moment without overarching goal, and where opportunity cost is constitutive of well-balanced game systems — without repercussions, actions lose their meaning.
dimension_operational_definitions.evidence_basis: verbatim-paraphrastic from Ch.3 p.44 dimension paragraph

KINESTHETIC.feature: Locus of attention is the control surface (avatar manipulation) rather than the environment itself
Foregrounded under unmastery or complex-sequence demand; recedes upon internalization
KINESTHETIC.distinguishes_from: all other dimensions (which do not exhibit the same control-presence/internalization dynamic in Ch.3)

KINESTHETIC.feature: Ergodic-dispositional under-determination: includes 'readiness to act' even when no physical input is occurring
KINESTHETIC.distinguishes_from: LUDIC (choice-and-repercussion), with which it can be confused under strategy-game cognitive-effort cases
KINESTHETIC.evidence_source: interview-informed (Red Orchestra sniper example, Ch.3 p.42)

KINESTHETIC.feature: Internalized state shows reduced attentional load measurable in resource-reallocation to other dimensions
KINESTHETIC.distinguishes_from: any dimension still fully consuming attentional resources

SPATIAL.feature: Locus is the virtual environment construed as a place to be inhabited, not the controls
Operative mode is navigation / exploration / spatial-internalization rather than narrative legibility
SPATIAL.distinguishes_from: NARRATIVE (where embedded objects and inhabitants generate story-significance rather than place-significance)
low-spatial games like Pong where the representation is too thin to support place-inhabitation
SPATIAL.evidence_source: interview + observation (the WoW Ratchet-to-Feathermoon route-planning case, Ch.3 p.42; the Pong / Oblivion / Half-Life 2 contrast, Ch.3 p.44)

SPATIAL.feature: Non-navigable spaces (FIFA stands, Battlefield 1942 outside-combat-area) are representational backdrop, NOT spatial-involvement loci
SPATIAL.distinguishes_from: the magic-circle-as-spatial-marker reading, which would treat all on-screen space as the same kind of space

SPATIAL.feature: Macro-phase signature: spatial mental models maintained off-line (e.g. Ratchet-to-Feathermoon route held in memory between sessions)
SPATIAL.distinguishes_from: kinesthetic macro signature (recalling avatar-control feats) which is anchored in the body schema rather than the place schema

SHARED.feature: Presence of other agents (human or computer-controlled) is the constitutive condition; remove the agents and the dimension drops out
SHARED.distinguishes_from: all other dimensions (which can operate in single-player isolation)

SHARED.feature: Includes ambient awareness of social context even absent direct interaction
SHARED.distinguishes_from: LUDIC under cooperative-play (where joint goal-pursuit could be misread as shared but is actually goal-structured)

SHARED.feature: Macro-phase signature: clan-website work, guild-political deliberation, persisting social bonds (mentioned as the majority macro-phase report in the interview data)
SHARED.distinguishes_from: narrative-macro signature (story-construction featuring one's character) which sits with NARRATIVE

SHARED.feature: Modalities span cohabitation / cooperation / competition — all three count, including non-collaborative awareness
SHARED.distinguishes_from: cooperative-only or competitive-only readings that would collapse SHARED into LUDIC

NARRATIVE.feature: Object of engagement is story-content (scripted) OR alterbiography-emergent story
Dual scripted / emergent character — both story-elements written into the game and those generated by the player's interaction with embedded objects, inhabitants, events
NARRATIVE.distinguishes_from: purely scripted-narrative reductions, which would miss the emergent component

NARRATIVE.feature: Macro-phase signature: speculating about a designed narrative's development; story-construction featuring one's character
Story-significance vs. place-significance of embedded objects: the same object can be loaded narratively or spatially depending on attentional foregrounding
NARRATIVE.distinguishes_from: SPATIAL (under environmental-storytelling, the boundary becomes contested — resolve via decision rule R3)

AFFECTIVE.feature: Object of engagement is the player's emotional state, irrespective of its trigger-dimension
AFFECTIVE.distinguishes_from: all other dimensions (which name the trigger-content rather than the emotional response itself)

AFFECTIVE.feature: Designer-installed (rhetorical strategies of affect) AND player-precipitated (individual interpretation) sources both count
AFFECTIVE.distinguishes_from: purely designer-side or purely player-side affect theories

AFFECTIVE.feature: Range spans calming aesthetic response, adrenaline-rush arousal, and uncanny — i.e. multi-valenced (not coextensive with positive affect / fun)
AFFECTIVE.distinguishes_from: fun-essentialism (excised) which collapses affective variation to one positive cluster
AFFECTIVE.evidence_source: theoretical inference (Ch.3 p.44; cross-referenced to the Fun? excision pp.51-53)

AFFECTIVE.feature: Macro-phase signature: sense of inner peace following travels in aesthetically moving surroundings; anticipatory excitement / anxiety about next session
AFFECTIVE.distinguishes_from: spatial-macro (route-planning, which is about navigation rather than the emotional residue of past navigation)

LUDIC.feature: Object of engagement is choice + repercussion + opportunity cost
Goal-source-agnostic: game-stipulated, player-stipulated, or community-stipulated goals all count; spur-of-the-moment decisions without overarching goal also count
LUDIC.distinguishes_from: Suits-style lusory-attitude readings (excised) which would tie ludic to voluntary-adoption-of-inefficient-means

LUDIC.feature: Repercussions-meaningfulness criterion: without repercussions, actions lose their meaning — choice-without-consequence is not ludic
LUDIC.distinguishes_from: free-form paidia (in Caillois's sense) which Salen+Zimmerman associate with the magic-circle paidia/ludus transition

LUDIC.feature: Macro-phase signature: winning-strategy formation, character-development planning, opportunity-cost rehearsal between sessions
LUDIC.distinguishes_from: narrative-macro (anticipating designed-narrative development), which is content-anticipation rather than choice-rehearsal

LUDIC.feature: Ergodic-disposition overlap with KINESTHETIC: strategy-game cognitive effort + sniper-readiness can be either dispositional ergodicity (kinesthetic readiness) or rehearsed choice-evaluation (ludic) — apply decision rule R1
LUDIC.evidence_source: theoretical inference (Ch.3 pp.41-42; the Empire: Total War + Red Orchestra cases)

ambiguous_case_decision_rules.ambiguous_pair: KINESTHETIC vs. LUDIC under strategy-game cognitive effort or sniper-waiting
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.rule: If the dispositional readiness is oriented toward execution of an action when conditions are met (e.g. firing on an enemy who appears), the case is KINESTHETIC. If the cognitive effort is the rehearsal / evaluation of choice-and-repercussion structures, the case is LUDIC. Cases like the Red Orchestra sniper (Ch.3 p.42) blend both; report both with weighting.
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.evidence_source: theoretical inference + interview-informed (Red Orchestra, Empire: Total War)

ambiguous_case_decision_rules.ambiguous_pair: SPATIAL vs. KINESTHETIC under heavy-navigation FPS games (e.g. Half-Life 2)
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.rule: If the player's attentional foregrounding is on the place-as-inhabited-environment (where am I, what is around me, how do I get to there), the case is SPATIAL. If it is on the controls / avatar-body manipulation (am I jumping correctly, am I aiming right), the case is KINESTHETIC. Internalized controls + foregrounded place = SPATIAL; foregrounded controls + recessed place = KINESTHETIC.

ambiguous_case_decision_rules.ambiguous_pair: SPATIAL vs. NARRATIVE under environmental-storytelling games (e.g. BioShock, Half-Life 2)
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.rule: If the player is attending to the environment-as-place-to-inhabit (route, layout, scale, atmosphere), the case is SPATIAL. If the player is attending to the environment-as-story-cipher (what does this room tell me about what happened, who lived here), the case is NARRATIVE. The same physical environment toggles between dimensions as attentional foregrounding shifts.
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.evidence_source: theoretical inference (Ch.3 pp.43-44; extending the layered-transparent principle)

ambiguous_case_decision_rules.ambiguous_pair: SHARED vs. LUDIC under cooperative goal-directed play
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.rule: If the engagement is driven by joint goal-pursuit and choice-coordination, code primarily LUDIC with SHARED as secondary modulator. If driven by social-context awareness, guild-political dynamics, or cohabitation independent of joint goal, code primarily SHARED. Cooperative strategy formation IS a joint case — both dimensions weighted.

AFFECTIVE always co-occurs with another dimension (which supplies the trigger); never code AFFECTIVE in isolation. Code AFFECTIVE as primary when the player's report or behavioral signature foregrounds the emotional response itself rather than the triggering content (e.g. 'the music made me cry' = AFFECTIVE primary; 'the boss fight was hard' = LUDIC + KINESTHETIC primary, AFFECTIVE secondary).
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.evidence_source: theoretical inference (Ch.3 p.44; reading the dimension as response-state rather than content-trigger)

ambiguous_case_decision_rules.ambiguous_pair: macro vs. micro phase under transitional / hinge cases
ambiguous_case_decision_rules.rule: If the activity is occurring during a gameplay session in front of the running game, code MICRO. If it is occurring off-line (between sessions, during commute, at bedtime, on community sites), code MACRO. Liminal cases like in-session map-consultation that interrupts gameplay are MICRO but with attention-direction toward the macro contextualization (e.g. the WoW Ratchet-to-Feathermoon planning is MICRO under Calleja's framing because the planning happens in-session over the in-game map).

If the analytic target is a discrete dimension-grain engagement (which dimension is operative, at what intensity), code at the INVOLVEMENT tier. If it is the higher-order integrated experiential phenomenon — sense of being-in-the-game — code at the PRESENCE/IMMERSION tier. Per Calleja, involvement must be modeled first; presence is the integrand of dimensional involvements over time.

methodology_specification.rationale_for_qualitative: intensely experiential and richly varied nature of the object of inquiry (Ch.3 p.36)
primary_methods: extended personal participation in the two selected game environments
in-depth interviews with twenty-five experienced players recruited in-game
supporting_methods: discussions with academics studying virtual worlds

interview_design.interview_location: within the virtual environment of the game about which the participant was being interviewed
interview_design.interview_location_rationale: to stimulate participant memory and to bring their relationship to the game world to the fore

analytical_procedure.procedure: data coded and analyzed between interviews; interview schedule updated in the intervening period to reflect input from participants
analytical_procedure.outcome_logic: over time a number of strong themes emerged; the player involvement model is based on these salient features of the data — the six dimensions correspond to the clusters of emphasis derived from analysis

methodology_specification.dissertation_relevance_note: This subsection is the dissertation's empirical-adaptation seed. The interview-within-the-game design + iterative coding + grounded-emergence of clusters is directly adaptable to the dissertation's planned game-analytic empirical chapter. Forebears (Taylor / Steinkuehler / Klastrup) are existing cross-pipeline anchors should be cross-referenced in future Phase 4 activation.
methodology_specification.extraction_confidence: high — single dense subsection captured in full

game_loci.analytic_use: MMORPG case-site for the underlying 3-year qualitative research (p.36); Ratchet-to-Feathermoon route-planning via in-game map = paradigm example of ergodicity-as-cognitive-effort within the micro phase (p.42)
MMOFPS case-site for the qualitative research, paired with WoW as the contrasting genre paradigm (p.36)
pedagogical fulcrum for the macro/micro distinction — in-session army-control + outmaneuvering = micro; bedtime tactical replay + commute campaign-mode strategy-planning = macro
worked example for ergodicity-as-readiness-to-act — sniper covering a street with no enemies in sight; Figure 3.2 reproduces this scene
low-spatial-involvement contrast case establishing that the model's dimensions need not all be present at high intensity in every game

game_loci.game: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (Bethesda Softworks, 2006)

game_loci.analytic_use: non-navigable stadium-stands = representational backdrop; refutes the spatial-marker function of the magic circle
non-navigable space outside combat area = representational backdrop; same point as FIFA 2009
physical golf = Suits's classic case of voluntary adoption of inefficient means; digital golf = counter-example because the rules are coded into the game and no voluntary adoption is needed
Salen+Zimmerman example for the transition from paidia (free play) to ludus (rule-bound game) via imposition of the magic circle's structured frame

tensions.summary: Anti-essentialist Wittgensteinian definitional posture vs. construction of a six-dimensional taxonomic apparatus
tensions.detail: Ch.1 commits the volume to a family-resemblance refusal of essentialist definitions of games; Ch.3 then offers a 6 x 2 grid that taxonomically organizes player experience. Calleja softens this by insisting the dimensions are layered + transparent rather than discrete, and that no game need exhibit all dimensions at high intensity — but the formal structure of the model remains taxonomic in shape.

tensions.summary: Bottom-up grounded-theoretic emergence of dimensions vs. presentation of dimensions as exhaustive of player experience
tensions.detail: Calleja states the dimensions are clusters derived from interview data — implying any future research could discover further dimensions or revise the present ones. But the chapter (and the book's chapter-architecture) treats the six dimensions as the complete inventory. Two MMOG case-sites is a thin empirical base for an exhaustive taxonomy of player experience.

tensions.summary: Macro vs. micro phase developmental asymmetry
tensions.detail: Macro exposition occupies ~pp.38-40 and is then largely absorbed into the dimension-chapter openings (Chs.4-9 each open with a macro-phase section). Micro exposition pp.40-43 is the chapter's analytic center of gravity and dominates the dimension chapters. The PIM is more elaborated micro-side than macro-side at the moment of its own introduction.

tensions.summary: Positive-constructive vs. negative-purgative work compressed into 20 pages
tensions.detail: The chapter must build a six-dimensional model with attentional-hierarchy grounding AND excise the magic-circle / lusory-attitude / fun apparatus in the same 20-page span. The negative-purgative work (pp.46-53) occupies nearly 40% of the chapter, structurally crucial but compressed.

tensions.summary: PIM as structural-taxonomic model vs. PIM as experiential-phenomenological description
tensions.detail: The model is presented diagrammatically (Figure 3.1's wagon-wheel) but the underlying phenomenology Calleja invokes — layered + transparent dimensions, fluid blending, dispositional readiness, ergodic cognitive effort — is continuous, gradient, non-discrete. The diagrammatic register and the experiential register pull against each other; the dissertation's adoption of the model should be aware that its instrument may need experiential rather than structural reading.

burke_pentad.rationale: Avatar / game-piece control is precisely the instrumental means by which the player Agent acts. The ergodic-dispositional reformulation strengthens this — Agency in Burke's sense includes the readiness/disposition of instrumentality, not just its physical exercise.
Place-as-inhabited is the Burkean Scene; the spatial-internalization process is the Agent's coming-to-dwell-in the Scene.
Other agents (human / computer) populate the dramatistic field; SHARED foregrounds the Agent-Agent ratios (cohabitation, cooperation, competition).
Story-content is the sequence of Acts toward Purposes, scripted and emergent; alterbiography is the emergent-Act layer.
Burke's later sixth-term (Attitude) captures the emotional-dispositional coloring of action; AFFECTIVE is precisely the response-state dimension.
Choice-and-repercussion within goal-structures is Purpose realized through Act; opportunity cost is the dramatistic weighting of alternative Acts.

uexkull_constructs.uexkull_construct: Funktionskreis (functional circle: Merkmal/Merkträger -> object -> Wirkmal/Wirkträger -> back to perception)
uexkull_constructs.rationale: The perception-action loop underlying avatar control IS a functional-circle structure: the player's perception of the control surface and on-screen state issues into action which alters the perceptual field; internalization is the closing of the loop into automaticity.

The virtual environment as inhabited-place is precisely Umwelt — the subjectively-constituted world of meaning-carriers; Merkwelt (perceptual world) and Wirkwelt (effect world) jointly compose the navigable virtual space.
Multiple agents inhabit overlapping but non-identical Umwelten; cohabitation, cooperation, and competition are biosemiotic modulations of overlap.
Scripted and emergent story-elements function as carriers of meaning serially encountered in the Umwelt; narrative is the player's reading of meaning-carrier sequence.

The qualitative coloring of perceived objects (their tone) is Uexküll's nearest construct to affective response; the multi-valenced affective range (calming / adrenaline / uncanny) maps onto differential tone-coloring.

uexkull_constructs.uexkull_construct: Wirkmal + goal-structure (effect-marker as condition for closure of functional circle)
uexkull_constructs.rationale: Ludic engagement is the choice-weighting that determines which effect-marker the player pursues; goals are organized effect-marker-closure conditions.

aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.rationale: Readiness-to-act is dunamis-as-hexis; learned-internalized control is the actualization of hexis. The Bowin AMT corpus index supplies the Aristotelian continuous-motion analysis.

aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.grounding_target: phantasia spatial-imagery (Phantasia Cluster — Hawhee rhetorical vision; Papachristou deliberative phantasia)
aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.rationale: Internalization of game-space is the maintenance of spatial phantasmata in memory between sessions; the macro-phase route-planning IS phantasia-deliberative.

aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.grounding_target: Mitsein (Heidegger BCAP) + the ethical-political register of phronesis
aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.rationale: Being-with as the ontological mode of co-inhabitation supplies the existential-analytic register that Calleja's social-context-awareness lacks.
Scripted-narrative engagement is engagement with muthos; alterbiography-emergent narrative is the player's emplotment-from-within.

aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.grounding_target: pathē (Aristotle Rhetoric II) + Gross 2017 Uncomfortable Situations + Uexküll Merktöne/Wirktöne
aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.rationale: Aristotelian pathē supply the systematic taxonomy Calleja's affective dimension lacks; Gross 2017's situated-emotion theory supplies the contemporary bridge.
Choice-and-repercussion under opportunity cost is the phronetic register; deliberative phantasia supplies the imagistic substrate of choice-rehearsal.

aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.grounding_target: BCAP kairos + ekstatic temporality + Bowin AMT continuous-time
aristotelian_heideggerian_grounding.rationale: Macro = anticipatory + retentional structure of player-being-toward-the-game; micro = ekstatic moment-to-moment engagement. BCAP and Bowin AMT supply the phenomenological-temporal vocabulary Calleja's relatively under-theorized macro/micro distinction needs.
